issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Animal has a constructor Animal(String, int) (i.e., name and age), but the provided solution implements Animal with a single-parameter constructor Animal(String). This constructor/parameter mismatch between the specification (UML) and the solution will confuse students about the required constructor signature and block following the UML-based instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent: either update the UML/problem statement to require Animal(String) (and adjust UML and textual references to remove age), or change the template and solution to implement Animal(String, int) (adding the age field and updating all concrete subclasses' constructors and any example usage such as Main). Ensure tests and example code match the chosen constructor signature.

issues.description: The UML and class diagram in the problem statement list Animal with two attributes (name: String and age: int), but elsewhere in the problem text and the solution the Animal only has/mentions a name. The age attribute is absent in the solution, producing an attribute-level mismatch between the specification and implementation and inconsistent guidance to students about which attributes to implement and provide getters/setters for.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify whether Animal should include an age attribute: if age is intended, update the template and solution to add a private int age field, include it in the constructor, and provide corresponding getter/setter; if age was included in the UML by mistake, update the UML and any textual mentions to remove age so all artifacts consistently require only a name attribute.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML declares Animal with attributes name:String and age:int and a constructor Animal(String, int), but the solution implements Animal with only a single-argument constructor Animal(String) and no age attribute. The template repository also does not provide an Animal class (comments in Farm.java reference Animal). This mismatch between the UML/requirements and the implemented constructor/signature can confuse students about the expected Animal API and which constructor to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the expected Animal constructor and attributes across artifacts. Either update the problem UML to specify Animal(String name) (removing age) or modify the solution and template to implement the age field with constructor Animal(String, int) and corresponding getter/setter so all artifacts use the same constructor signature and attributes.
